artworks.initial_prompt: Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: original professional game-development concept board for CINDER Act 3, TORMANCE — THE FALSE WORLD, inspired by David Lindsay's A Voyage to Arcturus (1920). Style/medium: carefully drawn tactile ink and gouache, strange early speculative-fiction imagination, strong silhouettes, sophisticated production design with six separated visual studies; generous gutters and clean restrained short labels. Landscape board roughly 3:2. Proposed game palette black, unnatural violet and sulphur-green with ivory highlights; respect any specifically mentioned novel colors. These colors/patterns are proposed equivalents for impossible colors, never a claim to literally render ulfire/jale. No lunar theatre, no modern science-fiction armor, no generic elves or medieval fantasy, no logos/watermarks, no graphic gore. Board should feel useful to environment and character artists. Exact costumes and architecture are adaptation proposals. Twelve separated full-body casting studies, 3 rows of 4 on pale paper. Source characters: MASKULL a giant broad robust man with heavy features, full black beard, short bristling black hair, tweed suit; NIGHTSpore lean middle-height, clean-shaven, wild distant eyes, tweeds; KRAG angular unsettling guide in ordinary period travel clothing (costume interpreted); BACKHOUSE short thickset pointed beard medium; MONTAGUE FAULL rich South-American merchant in an early-1900 lounge suit; MRS JAMESON refined small patrician pianist; KENT-SMITH elderly bright-eyed former magistrate; PRIOR genial coffee importer; LANG tall thinning bald stockbroker; PROFESSOR HALBART small meagre psychologist; MRS TRENT tall graceful black-haired woman in expensive evening dress; the unnamed luminous séance MATERIALISATION as a still uncanny human figure. Clothing early twentieth-century civilian, no astronaut suits. Small bottom strip of traveler pixel-silhouette translation proposals, not replacement costumes for all cast. Character demeanor differentiated, no generic warrior squad. Labels just names.
